Welcome
Welcome to Emerson Valley School and to our school websiteAt Emerson Valley, we encourage all of our children to aspire to be independent, resilient, lifelong learners who have the skills to adapt to the changing world around them. They have respect for each other, themselves and our community. To be the best they can be as global citizens, we aim to develop socially aware individuals who understand the impact they can have on others. Mrs Hayley White | Headteacher
5 Dimensions Trust
We are a Multi-Academy Trust that serves the young people of west Milton Keynes, currently comprising of three secondary schools; The Hazeley Academy, Shenley Brook End School and Walton High and three primary schools; Priory Rise School, Emerson Valley School and Merebrook Infant School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Emerson Valley School - Breakfast and After School Clubs
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Clubs
Our wrap around care is run by Emerson Valley School directly. This means the staff get to know the children during the day and in the breakfast and afterschool clubs. We make sure that the clubs run seamlessly and congruently with our school rules, values and expectations. We know that our children will need some time after and before school to be themselves and it is not a continuation of academic education and so we lead activities in which the children can express and enjoy themselves. We also support with homework and will give the children the opportunity to complete this.
We are lucky at the moment that parents are able to book the sessions they want for both clubs and there is no need to book an entire term in advance. (This may change in the future if the clubs get full.)
Breakfast club
Cost £4.50 (£5 from September 2026)
Breakfast club is open from 07:45 and the children can come and play, read or chat. If they would like there is breakfast served until 08:30. Breakfast consists of a selection of cereals, toast, fruit, yoghurts and occasionally pastries or croissants.
At the end of the session children are supervised to go and line up with their friends and enter school to at the start of the school day.
This club is currently subsidised if your child is entitled to FSM/PP –there is no charge for attending.
Please drop your child to the reception and make sure they are handed over to a member of staff. No child should arrive before 07:45, the doors to reception will not be open before this time and your child will not be able to gain access to the school.
Afterschool club
Cost £11.50 (£12 from September 2026)
At afterschool club there are a variety of activities offered. Children can play games, complete craft activities, finish homework, read, use iPads, watch TV, sing Karaoke, play outside or play games in the hall. We vary the activities depending on the needs of the children on the day, the weather, the number of attendees and whether it is a theme day.
There is a healthy snack served. This might be things like open sandwiches or wraps with cheese, ham or egg mayonnaise, vegetable battons, fruit platters or yoghurts. Sometimes there is hot food available like potato wedges or pasta bake. In the hot weather the children have enjoyed ice lollies. All food follows the schools healthy eating guidelines.
Please collect your child from the reception. Children will only be handed over to those named on Arbor for collection.
Late collections and fees
The club closes at 18:00. If you are late collecting your child you will be charged at £5 for every 5 minutes that you are late collecting. If you are late on more than 2 occasions in a term your child’s bookings may be cancelled and any outstanding monies (less the late fees) will be refunded to you. We reserve the right to update this condition at any time. We will notify all parents with future bookings if we do update it, and you would have the right to withdraw your child from future sessions with a full refund.
Booking Details
Emergency contact number 07960 403440 – to use when the school office is closed
Clubs must be paid for in advance.

Whilst we can’t guarantee everybody their first choice of club, we do try to ensure all children that want to join a club are offered one. Clubs currently take place from 3:25-4:25 in the evenings. There is a small charge for our clubs which covers the cost of running them.

Admissions
The 5 Dimension admission policy for our school is available here: Admissions Policy
The admissions for Emerson Valley school are all coordinated by Milton Keynes council. The website for this is:
https://www.milton-keynes.gov.uk/schools-and-lifelong-learning/school-admissions
The council website will give you the opportunity to apply for a school place and details the admissions procedures we follow as a school.
If you would like to book a visit or talk further about our school, please contact our Office team on 01908 507914.
The defined area/catchment for our school is Emerson Valley and Furzton.
As we are a Junior school, children start our school in Year 3. If you are looking for a school for Reception, Year 1 or Year 2 please see the website for Merebrook Infant School one of the infant schools that feeds us and is also part of the 5 Dimension Trust.
Children are also admitted to other year groups throughout the year as long as there are places available.
The Local Authority School Admissions Team co-ordinate all school admissions. They process all applications and will contact you to let you know if a place has been allocated.

Should you wish to appeal against the decision not to offer your child a place at Emerson Valley School, please email office@EVS5D.com providing the name of the child, date of birth, and email address where the form to appeal can be sent.

Mathematics
“A high-quality mathematics education therefore provides a foundation for understanding the world, the ability to reason mathematically, an appreciation of the beauty and power of mathematics, and a sense of enjoyment and curiosity about the subject.
National Curriculum 2014
Intent
Emerson Valley School is committed to helping pupils become fluent in mathematics, reason mathematically, and apply their knowledge to problem-solving. The school emphasises the real-world importance of maths, fostering confidence and enjoyment in the subject. Their goal is for students to achieve mastery through deep, lasting understanding while developing curiosity and appreciation for the beauty and power of mathematics.
Impact
Emerson Valley School is committed to helping pupils become fluent in mathematics, reason mathematically, and apply their knowledge to problem-solving. The school emphasises the real-world importance of maths, fostering confidence and enjoyment in the subject. Their goal is for students to achieve mastery through deep, lasting understanding while developing curiosity and appreciation for the beauty and power of mathematics.
Implementation
Maths at Emerson Valley follows the 2014 National Curriculum and the Teaching for Mastery approach, using White Rose Maths for Years 3 to 6. Lessons are structured sequentially, with small, connected steps building on prior learning. A concrete, pictorial, and abstract approach helps pupils develop conceptual understanding.
Teachers use scaffolding, questioning, rapid intervention, and enrichment activities to support all learners. Most pupils progress at a similar pace, with advanced learners tackling complex problems and those needing more support receiving additional practice. Gaps in understanding are addressed within and outside lessons. Consistency in teaching is ensured through high-quality resources.
Impact
The curriculum's impact on pupils' development is assessed both formatively and summatively through regular teacher assessments, NFER, and past SATs tests. In-school moderation by year group teams, the Mathematics leader, and senior leaders ensures consistent progress. Teaching and learning are monitored to maintain high standards. By the end of Year 6, pupils are well-prepared for secondary school and beyond in their mathematical journey.

Music
“Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. A high-quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement.” National Curriculum 2014
Intent
Our curriculum empowers children to become musicians by: Performing, listening to, and evaluating diverse music from various historical periods, genres, and styles.
Singing, composing, using instruments, and leveraging technology to enhance their musical skills.
Exploring music creation, production, and communication through key musical elements like pitch, dynamics, and notation.
Implementation
Music skills are taught once a week during music lessons and pupils also engage in a singing assembly once a week. Lessons are planned with clear outlines of knowledge and vocabulary that children must master throughout their time at the school, ensuring progression and depth. Formal assessments take place at the end of each unit of work through performances and written compositions as well as ongoing assessment throughout units of work to ensure a depth to the pupils understanding.
Impact
The Music curriculum at Emerson Valley is designed to promote steady progress, enabling children to excel in their musical abilities. Students will learn to play and compose for various instruments, including recorder, keyboard, and guitar, as well as perform in large ensembles. As students gain confidence, they will improve their performance skills, develop a deeper understanding of music analysis using the Elements of Music, and be able to compose across different genres and instruments.

There is a whole school assembly on a Monday and a Friday morning at 9:05am. Throughout the week, there are other assemblies in class, in year groups or in phases.

Culinera are delighted to work with Emerson Valley School to provide the catering service within your school restaurant. You can find out everything you need to know about this terms food, special events and how to contact us here.
We look forward to welcoming you!

Free School Meal (FSM) Funding is available for children who qualify to pay for school meals. To see if your child is eligible, please fill the form in here: Online Free School Meals . If your child is entitled this will also attract other additional funding for their school to support their education.
Currently all children at Merebrook Infant School receive Universal Infant Free School Meals (UIFSM). This is an automatic entitlement and will end once you finish Year 2. If you are likely to be eligible for the FSM funding, please apply as soon as you can using this link Online Free School Meals

Not only are there the obvious health and social benefits of sitting down together to enjoy a cooked meal, this represents a significant cost saving to families. In addition, the children will be given a packed lunch when attending a school trip.
If you are not entitled to FSM or UIFSM and do not wish to purchase a lunch then you can send your child in with a healthy packed lunch. Please send your child in the morning with their lunch packed into a small lunch box or bag – ideally an insulated bag which will help to keep the lunch cool.
The only drink we allow at school is water so please do not send other drinks or your child will not be allowed to drink them.
For lunch ideas see Lunchbox ideas and recipes – Healthier Families - NHS
Our schools are nut free as we do have children with severe nut allergies. Do not send any products containing nuts into school, this includes for example cereal bars with nuts, peanut and other nut butters in sandwiches or wraps, pesto on pasta. Chocolate spread also often contains hazelnuts so please don’t send any products which include chocolate spread.

School Uniform
What to wear
Wearing school uniform establishes a strong group identity and sense of equality and helps to create a purposeful working environment. We encourage all children to take pride in their appearance and all children are expected to arrive for school smartly dressed in their school uniform. We believe a uniform helps to establish a strong community identity and supports the purposeful learning environment. The school is committed to working with parents to ensure that the correct uniform is worn by all children.
Please see our dress code policy for details of the uniform for each school. Dress Code Policy . (There is a section for Merebrook Infant School, one for Emerson Valley School - note that Year 6 pupils wear a different colour sweatshirt.)
Please note that the only branded item we ask you to purchase is the Jade green PE T-Shirt for Emerson Valley School. All other items can be branded or unbranded depending on your choice.
The branded items can be purchased directly from Kedaph Schoolwear via the link below or by visiting their shop. The remaining uniform items such as trousers, skirts and plain polo tops may be purchased either at the Kedaph shop or at a wide variety of stores.
Kedaph Schoolwear Ltd
Unit A Lennox Road Bletchley Milton Keynes MK2 2HH
In order to give parents an alternative to purchasing new uniform, we hold regular second hand uniform sales in school.
Naming Uniform
One of the biggest frustrations from parents is uniform not looked after by children and going missing. Please help your child out by labelling everything they bring into school including; coats, jumpers, PE jumpers, water bottles, lunch boxes, bags, trainers and shoes.
There are many ways to label items; stick in labels, permanent marker, sew in labels, stamps. Which ever you chose please check that the label is on the item before sending it back into school. If necessary name the item again. It is not easy to reunite a child with a burgundy school jumper when every child has the same one.

pageCache.text:
Travel to school
At Emerson Valley we encourage sustainable travel to school. We like to see our pupils walking, scooting or cycling. Most of our pupils live within a 20 minute was of the school. It's a great way to start the day with some activity, it reduces emissions around the school and reduces the traffic.
Morning Walking Bus: If you have another child who goes to Merebrook Infant School your Emerson Valley pupil can join the walking bus at 08:30 next to Merebrook School where they are walked over by 2 members of staff.
The map below shows the 5 minute and 10 minute walking zones to Emerson Valley School. If you do need to use a car, please can we encourage you to park in the blue zone and walk the final bit to school. This not only helps with congestion but also gives your child some healthy exercise in the morning.

Reading
“The overarching aim for English in the national curriculum is to promote high standards of language and literacy by equipping pupils with a strong command of the spoken and written language, and to develop their love of literature through widespread reading for enjoyment.” (DfE 2013)
Intent
Emerson Valley School prioritises reading at the core of its curriculum, aiming to immerse students in quality texts and diverse authors. The goal is to foster a love for reading, encouraging frequent and varied reading for both enjoyment and learning. By the time they leave, students will be fluent, confident readers prepared for secondary education and lifelong learning.
Implementation
The curriculum includes high-quality texts to enhance learning across subjects. Children participate in daily Guided Reading sessions, using the VIPERS approach (Vocabulary, Infer, Predict, Explain, Retrieve) to develop reading skills. They are introduced to quality authors through daily story times, and a weekly lesson is dedicated to fostering a love of reading. Reading is further promoted through events like World Book Day and visits from authors and illustrators.
Impact
Pupils will have a good knowledge of a range of authors and genres including classics and poetry and read widely and often with fluency, comprehension and enjoyment. Children of all abilities will be competent readers who have the necessary reading skills to achieve well at school and are able to transfer and apply these throughout the wider curriculum and when they move up to Secondary education.
